messages:
Sarah (Support): Hey team, customer (AcmeApp) is hitting flaky SSE behavior on our hosted API. They report streams disconnecting after ~60s-90s with partial JSON/event payloads. Client reconnects show duplicated events or truncated last object. They see no 5xx from our API — the client sees a TCP FIN. Ticket: #C-5429.

Sarah (Support): Repro steps from customer:
1) Connect using EventSource in browser to https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?session=abc
2) Receive 2-3 events, then stream stalls for ~60s, then connection closes.
3) Client automatically reconnects; on reconnect they sometimes see the last event partially repeated (truncated JSON like '{"id": 123, "text": "Hello W') or an empty final event.

Headers they captured:
- Content-Type: text/event-stream
- Cache-Control: no-cache
- Connection: keep-alive
- Transfer-Encoding: chunked

They called out that they sit behind Cloudflare and an internal ALB in front of us.

Mike (Infra): Thanks — can you ask them for a raw curl -v -N capture, and any platform-level logs? Also which target type on the ALB (IP vs instance) and whether there's an NLB in front of the ALB? ALB default idle timeout is 60s which could explain a 60s close.

Sarah (Support): Got curl output from customer (redacted):
```
$ curl -v -N 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?session=abc'
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (1.2.3.4) port 443 (#0)
> GET /v1/stream?session=abc HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.ai
> User-Agent: curl/7.68.0
> Accept: */*
>
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< content-type: text/event-stream
< transfer-encoding: chunked
< cache-control: no-cache
<
data: {"id":1}

data: {"id":2}

# then nothing for ~60s
* Connection #0 to host api.redwood.ai left intact
* Received HTTP/2 stream 0 was reset: CANCEL
* Closing connection 0
```
(They also captured a TLS close from their browser: `net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET` intermittently.)

Carlos (SRE): This looks like classic proxy/balancer-induced buffering/idle termination + client reconnect interaction. A few likely culprits in order:
- ALB idle timeout set to 60s (default) and the stream saw no bytes for that interval so ALB closed the connection. ALB will send a FIN, client sees reset.
- Cloudflare (if enabled) can buffer or transform responses unless the origin sets headers that prevent buffering/transform. Cloudflare historically buffers streaming responses unless the origin sends proper SSE headers and avoids content-length.
- Envoy/nginx in our stack might be buffering upstream or have low `idle_timeout`/`proxy_read_timeout` causing early closes or upstream resets.
- Chunking details: if an intermediate sets a Content-Length or rewrites Transfer-Encoding, buffering can appear as partial outputs.

Carlos (SRE): Quick triage items for us to correlate:
- Check ALB target group idle timeout (should be >= expected keepalive gap or set a heartbeat).
- Check our Envoy route/cluster `idle_timeout`, `upstream_idle_timeout`, and `max_connection_duration` values.
- Check nginx `proxy_buffering` and `proxy_read_timeout` if we're using nginx as a reverse proxy.
- Check logs for `upstream reset` or `connection termination` entries in Envoy logs and SRE traces.

Mike (Infra): I pulled Envoy logs for that customer's requests around the reported ts: found repeated lines like:
```
[warning] upstream reset: connection termination
[info] downstream remote close
```
Suggests the downstream (ALB/Cloudflare) closed first. Also saw repeated 502 spikes upstream when we tried to re-create with curl via our test harness (we have an ALB in front of Envoy).

Carlos (SRE): Repro suggestions for the customer and our internal test: use these 3 tests to isolate layer:
1) Direct curl to origin instance (bypass ALB/Cloudflare) — curl -v -N to origin IP:443. If stream stays up, LB is at fault.
2) Curl via ALB (no Cloudflare) — if this fails at ~60s, ALB timeout likely.
3) Curl via Cloudflare + ALB — if behavior changes (buffering / chunk delays), Cloudflare origin buffering step is in play.

Provide client-side reprod steps (EventSource/node):
```
# Node quick SSE client that prints connect/disconnect
const EventSource = require('eventsource');
const es = new EventSource('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?session=abc');
es.onmessage = (e) => console.log('MSG', e.data);
es.onerror = (err) => console.log('ES error', err);

# curl repro
curl -v -N 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?session=abc'
```

Mike (Infra): Short-term mitigation we can ask customer to try: implement a small SSE heartbeat from client or server (send a `:\n` or `: ping` comment every 15s). Also ask Cloudflare to disable response buffering for this route or add `Cache-Control: no-transform`. Increase ALB idle timeout to 180s as an immediate workaround.

Carlos (SRE): Config snippets (internal notes) — nginx fronting the app (if used) should include: 
```
# nginx upstream config
proxy_buffering off;
proxy_cache off;
proxy_set_header Connection ""; # allow chunked / keep-alive passthrough
proxy_http_version 1.1;
proxy_set_header Host $host;
proxy_read_timeout 300s;
proxy_send_timeout 300s;
chunked_transfer_encoding on;
```
For Envoy, check route/cluster timeouts; example route patch: 
```
# envoy route fragment (illustrative)
"route": {
  "idle_timeout": "0s",          # disable route-level idle close
  "cluster": "sse_backend"
}
# cluster config: ensure connection and health timeouts are generous
```
(We kept this intentionally high-level — we will use the infra playbook to apply exact patches.)

Carlos (SRE): Cloudflare specifics: ensure origin returns `Content-Type: text/event-stream` and avoid `Content-Length`. Add `Cache-Control: no-transform` and `Connection: keep-alive`. Cloudflare may still buffer in some products; if they use Cloudflare Workers or proxied features, they may need to enable the option that supports streaming or use a route that bypasses caching.

Mike (Infra): I pushed a quick test change in staging that sends a tiny comment heartbeat every 20s from the streaming service and bumped nginx `proxy_read_timeout` to 240s in the staging proxy. Verified curl -N to staging through ALB stayed open for >5m without ALB forcing a close because I also increased ALB idle timeout on the staging target group.

DeployBot: deploy v2025.11.02-staging-heartbeat succeeded to staging (sha: a1b2c3).

Sarah (Support): I messaged the customer with the triage steps and recommended they:
- Test direct to origin to rule out ALB/Envoy.
- Ask their Cloudflare admin to disable buffering on that route or set `no-transform`.
- If they can't change Cloudflare, add a client-side reconnect/backoff with Last-Event-ID dedupe.
- We can temporarily increase ALB idle timeout for their target group if they want us to (we control hosted ALB).

Sarah (Support): Customer responded: direct-to-origin works stable, ALB->origin is where the disconnect happens at ~60s. They asked us to increase ALB idle timeout for their target group.

Carlos (SRE): Action items:
- [x] Increase ALB idle timeout for the customer's target group to 180s (done)
- [x] Add server-side SSE heartbeat option behind a feature flag (staging deploy verifies)
- [ ] Follow-up with infra to audit Envoy `idle_timeout` config across LB-ed routes and raise if needed
- [ ] Document standard SSE checklist for support runbook (nginx/Envoy/ALB/Cloudflare tips)

Sarah (Support): Marking customer ticket as "investigating -> mitigated" and adding notes about ALB idle timeout. Will keep ticket open until customer confirms stability for 24h.

Carlos (SRE): Long-term: we should add an automated internal test that runs a 10-minute SSE through the full network path (Cloudflare/ALB/Envoy/app) to detect regressions and ensure idle timeouts and buffering behavior are correct. Also add a snippet to our docs about SSE headers and how to preflight Cloudflare/ALB settings.

Sarah (Support): Thanks all. I'll update the runbook and ping infra for the Envoy audit.

(End of thread)
